one_month_reasoning: In the window to 2026-11-19: Q3 2026 results (date not announced; ~2026-11-04 after close by analogy with 2025-11-05). Q3 is usually Centrus's smallest delivery quarter (FY revenue guide $450-500M vs H1 $252.8M puts most of H2 in Q4), and advanced-technology costs and stock comp are rising, so a weak Q3 print is expected and the guide reaffirmation matters more; possible news on the pending 2026-27 Russian import waiver, TENEX export licences and post-2026-09-30 HALEU cascade arrangements. The Investor Day (December 2026) is outside the window. The stock is down 37% since early September with ~30% of float short, so a reversal and further momentum are both live. No strong signal: a near-symmetric lognormal centred at ~$108.5 with monthly vol 0.25 (89%/3.5), very slightly below spot for the negative sector momentum.

thesis_break_reason: $40 is about net cash at the horizon plus the DOE-funded HALEU leg (~$17.5 floor + ~$23 HALEU rNPV per share). Trading there would mean the market doubts even the government-backed HALEU build or the cash: a DOE funding cut, a Piketon halt or a dilutive rescue raise, i.e. something fundamental, not volatility. On the upside, sustained trading above ~$190 with a disclosed capex/SWU below ~$800 and term SWU above $250 would break my bearish thesis.

reasoning: Industry lane. The rest of the chain says enrichment is tight but new capacity is expensive: Urenco's order book rose to EUR27.3B and spot SWU sits at $200 (Urenco H1-26), term ~$180 (Silex, Aug-26), yet US utilities paid only $108.70/SWU on average in 2025 (EIA) because contracts lag, and Urenco itself earns ~38-47% EBITDA margins (FY2025; S&P 2027 forecast). Against that, building new centrifuge capacity costs ~$676/SWU-yr at Orano's 7.4M SWU scale and ~$1,400 on the inflation-adjusted ACP history, and DOE had to put $2.7B behind three projects (Centrus, Orano, General Matter) to get them built. A 16M+ SWU Western wave (Orano IKE 2032-39, GLE from 2030, Urenco +2.8M) lands just as Centrus ramps. Centrus today is a trader: 'well over one-half' of 2027 deliveries are TENEX-sourced, US waivers end 2027-12-31, so FY2028 is a gap year before Piketon's 2029 first output; the engine therefore runs no DCF and the value sits in an rNPV SOTP. My build (1.2M SWU LEU at $195, 12 MTU HALEU at $350/SWU, ~$2.1B phase-1 capex, DOE $900M milestones at p0.85) gives LEU -$197M, HALEU +$544M, expansion option +$27M, plus run-off, Westerman, TS, corporate cost and $400M net cash at H: SOTP $33.12; market-share scenarios $67.8 and cash floor + option $43.0 bracket it; fair value $47.44. Reverse DCF: today's price needs ~2.8x my base EBITDA, close to my bull case (p0.30). For the ladder I do not assume the market converges to my value within 12 months: prices beat fundamentals as 12-month forecasts, the December Investor Day can show better capex/price economics than my low-confidence estimates, nuclear names carry a sentiment premium, and short interest is ~30%. I put a median of ~$80 (about 55% weight on spot in log terms), lognormal sigma 0.75 (below the 89% realised vol, which included the 2025-26 bubble), giving P(>= $110) = 0.336. Research limits: Centrus's August 2026 investor deck returned 403, so its capacity figures were not used; HALEU pricing basis and phase-1 capex are estimates.

custom.name: Cash floor + Piketon call option (e)
custom.explanation: Cash floor plus Piketon as a call option. Floor at H: net cash $400M + legacy trading run-off $85M + Westerman $100M + TS $30M - corporate cost PV $198M = $417M / 23.87M sh = $17.5. Option: underlying S = unrisked PV at H of Piketon LEU ($505M) + HALEU operating cash ($435M) + DOE task-order milestones ($706M PV at 10%) = $1.65B (from the rNPV parts); strike K = PV at 10% of remaining phase-1 capex $1.13B = $0.98B; sigma 45% (term SWU went from ~$60 in 2020 to ~$180 in 2026; below the 89% equity vol because the equity is levered to the project); T = 2 yrs (go/no-go on LEU cascades before 2029 first output); r = 4.0%. Black-Scholes: d1 = (ln(1.646/0.978) + (0.04 + 0.45^2/2) x 2) / (0.45 x sqrt2) = 1.26, d2 = 0.63; C = 1,646 x 0.897 - 978 x e^-0.08 x 0.734 = $813M, x 0.75 demand/technical success (HALEU demand p0.65, LEU book p0.9) = $610M / 23.87M = $25.5. Total $17.5 + $25.5 = $43.0.

bear.story: Piketon slips past 2030 and over budget (capex/SWU toward the inflation-adjusted ACP history), HALEU demand from advanced reactors lags (NRC/FOAK delays), the 2026-27 Russian waiver or TENEX licences fail, and DOE milestones slip; pos -35%, volumes -15%, custom legs -45%, EV/sales -1.0x, rate +1pt.

base.story: Phase 1 (12 MTU HALEU + ~1.2M SWU LEU) starts in late 2029 and ramps to 2033; realised LEU SWU ~$195 and HALEU SWU ~$350; Urenco-like 45-47% margins; DOE milestones paid; the legacy TENEX/Orano trading book runs off by 2030.

bull.story: Term SWU rises toward $240-260 as the Russian ban bites before Orano/GLE/Urenco additions (2030-2039) arrive, HALEU demand reaches DOE's 50 MT/yr path, Centrus exercises the expansion to ~3.5M SWU in existing buildings; pos +20%, volumes/prices +50%, custom legs +90%, EV/sales +1.5x.

model_inputs.structure_note: Value is carried by an explicit sum of the parts (weight 0.45) whose core is rNPV of the Piketon build (LEU contingent book; HALEU 12 MTU with the $900M DOE task order milestones as probability-weighted negative development costs; expansion option), plus a cash-flow run-off of the legacy TENEX/Orano trading book, Westerman at near cost, Technical Solutions, and a negative corporate-cost part; two custom legs (market-share scenarios 0.25, cash floor + option 0.20) and a capped EV/sales cross-check (0.10). The three consolidated years (FY2026-28) describe the existing business only (expansion capex sits in rNPV dev costs after the horizon and in net_debt_horizon before it). FY2028 is the gap year between the end of Russian LEU imports to the US (waivers end 2027-12-31) and first Piketon output (2029), so core NOPAT is negative and the engine sets the DCF weight to 0 (pre-profit rule); the plant's cash flows are valued in rNPV rather than by fading a trough year.
model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian: (1) phase-1 capex of ~$2.1B total (~$1,235 per SWU/yr, between Orano IKE's ~$676 at 7.4M SWU scale and the inflation-adjusted ~$1,430 of the original ACP) is my estimate: the company only says 'multi-billion' and may disclose it at the December 2026 Investor Day; each -$300M of capex adds ~+$11/share. (2) HALEU priced on SWU (customer-supplied feed) at $350/SWU vs $415/SWU implied by DOE's $17.0M/MTU option price; if Centrus must buy natural feed (~42 kgU per kg HALEU) HALEU margins collapse. (3) DCF weight 0 because the FY2028 core is a trough by construction (Russian import ban, no Piketon output yet). (4) No `contracts` entry: the $900M DOE task order is milestone-paid against capacity deployment and carried in the HALEU rNPV with p0.85. (5) fair_value.value equals the engine base horizon value.

LEU segment roughly flat (TENEX deliveries under waivers through 2027; RPO $0.7B LEU to 2030) plus ~$70M of Westerman third-party revenue (est. ~$90M on ~400 employees less intercompany casings); HALEU operations revenue ends (DOE Option 1b maintenance only).
inputs_detail.variant_view: If Westerman is smaller (~$50M) growth is +4%; value effect <$1/share as the core is valued mainly through net cash.

inputs_detail.derivation: US import ban leaves no waivers after 2027-12-31 and 'well over one-half' of LEU delivered through 2027 is TENEX-sourced (10-Q); LEU revenue falls to ~$230M (Orano supply to 2030, TENEX for non-US customers, inventory) from ~$340M; Westerman/TS ~$170M.
inputs_detail.variant_view: A pre-2028 stockpile of waiver-volume LEU could hold 2028 LEU revenue near $300M (+$15M GP).

inputs_detail.derivation: FY2026: H1 GAAP EBIT $11.2M + H2 ~$13M = ~$24M (5%). FY2027: LEU GP ~ $110M (FY2025 LEU GP $111.5M) less SG&A+SBC ~$60M, advanced technology ~$25M, amortisation ~$5M -> ~$18M. FY2028: LEU GP ~$58M (25% on $230M) + TS $3M + Westerman $7M - $85M corporate/adv tech -> ~-$16M.
FY2025 tax $8.1M on pretax $85.9M = 9%; NOL carryforwards (Section 382 rights plan) keep cash tax low; 15% blended.

inputs_detail.input: D&A / capex / SBC % of core revenue
inputs_detail.derivation: D&A FY2025 $9.9M (2.2%); maintenance capex only (FY2023-24 $1.6-4.1M; expansion capex carried in rNPV/net_debt_horizon); SBC FY2025 $5.7M but Q2 2026 stock comp $17.7M (call) -> ~$21M/yr = 4.5%.

Cash $1,868.5M (6/30) - convert principal $1,207.5M ($402.5M 2.25% 2030 + $805.0M 0% 2032) = $661M; + ~$489M net September offering - $95M Westerman cash - ~$125M Q3 capex/advanced-technology spend = ~$930M.

Start $930M; minus ~$700M expansion spend Oct-2026 to Oct-2027 (Q4-26 ~$150M to land in the $350-500M 2026 capital-deployment guide; 2027 ~$700M x 0.8); plus core operating cash ~$60M, net interest ~$45M (4% on ~$1.7B average cash less the 2.25% coupon, after tax), DOE milestones ~$60M before H = ~$395M.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Faster 2027 spend ($900M) leaves ~$240M net cash (-$7/share), offset by plant value in rNPV.

inputs_detail.derivation: 19,233,908 Class A (424B5) + 500,000 offered + 719,200 Class B + 2,005,513 pre-funded warrants + ~0.165M Westerman shares ($21M / ~$127) = 22.62M; + 0.47M net shares from the in-the-money 2.25% 2030 notes at $109.88 (402.5/97.50 = 4.128M x (1 - 97.50/109.88)); + ~0.3M RSU/SAR = 23.4M. Common warrants (6.99M at $226.86-362.98) out of the money.

inputs_detail.derivation: Peer EV/sales TTM: BWXT 3.9x, CEG 4.7x, ASPI 3.8x (run peer table); set below the peer median ~4.3x because Centrus's core revenue is pass-through SWU trading at 25-30% gross margin.

Contingent LEU book ~$3.0B ($2.4B definitive) delivered ~2029-2040 = ~$260M/yr; at ~$195 realised (term ~$180 Aug 2026 per Silex, spot $200 June 2026 per Urenco, book signed 2023-25 at lower prices with escalation) ~1.2-1.35M SWU; 1.2M used.
inputs_detail.variant_view: If the book is mostly SWU at $230 the peak is ~$280M (+$70M rNPV, +$3/share).

inputs_detail.derivation: S&P forecasts Urenco EBITDA EUR900-1,000M on EUR1,900-2,100M revenue in 2027 (~47%); Urenco FY2025 38.4% at lagging realised prices; new plant has low sustaining capex: 45% cash margin.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Subscale plant with Urenco-like tails/decommissioning costs could run 35% (-$65M rNPV).

inputs_detail.value: 2029-10-01, 4-yr ramp to 2033; p = 0.85 build x 0.90 book firming = 0.765
inputs_detail.derivation: 10-Q: first new centrifuges online in Ohio in 2029; ANS: first new commercial capacity by 2029. Build probability reflects proven AC100M design but Centrus/USEC history (ACP abandoned 2009 after >$2.6B spent, WNA); 0.90 that contingent commitments convert.

inputs_detail.input: Phase-1 capex remaining after H (LEU / HALEU)
inputs_detail.derivation: Phase 1 ~1.7M SWU (1.2M LEU + ~0.49M SWU for 12 MTU HALEU at 41 SWU/kg) x ~$1,235/SWU = ~$2.1B (between Orano IKE ~$5B / 7.4M SWU = $676 and original ACP $3.5B / 3.8M SWU = $920 in mid-2000s dollars x ~1.55 = ~$1,430); ~$0.97B spent by H (FY2025 $19.7M + 2026 ~$385M + 0.8 x 2027 $700M) leaves ~$1.13B, split 2/3 LEU; spend probability 0.9.
inputs_detail.variant_view: If Investor Day shows ~$1.5B total, remaining capex falls ~$0.6B (+$22/share).

inputs_detail.derivation: 12 MTU/yr initial capacity (ANS/10-Q); 41.0 SWU per kg at 19.75% from natural feed with 0.25% tails (my calculation); DOE options $17.0M per MTU = $415/SWU if feed is customer-supplied, haircut to $350 for commercial buyers.
inputs_detail.variant_view: If Centrus must supply feed (~42.3 kgU/kg at ~$300/kgU = $12.7k/kg), the $17k/kg DOE price leaves little margin and the HALEU leg falls by ~$250M.

inputs_detail.derivation: DOE: demand could reach 50 MT/yr by 2035, but Oklo's LOI is non-binding and advanced-reactor fleets are pre-licence; X-energy definitive offtake delivers from 2030. 50% margin on a premium SWU price in small criticality-constrained cascades.

Firm fixed price $900.0M paid as milestones are met; ~40% in 2028 and ~30% at completion of the initial phase in 2031 (10-Q); the remaining ~30% spread 2027-2030 with ~$60M before H. Entered as negative development costs in the HALEU rNPV.
inputs_detail.variant_view: FY2027 budget does not fund cascade operation; appropriations risk is in p0.85.

inputs_detail.derivation: Project-level nominal rate below the ~11% cost of equity (10-yr ~5.3% + premium on a high beta) because DOE milestones and contracted volumes are lower risk; technical/market risk is in the phase probabilities.

inputs_detail.value: peak $504M (1.8M SWU x $280), margin 58%, capex $1.4B 2030-32, p 0.30
inputs_detail.derivation: Original ACP licence was 3.8M SWU; extra 1.8M SWU in existing buildings at ~$780/SWU (Oak Ridge factory already built). Only exercised in a high-price state; at $260/SWU it is NPV-neutral at 11%, so I use $280 and p0.30 (Western additions: Urenco USA +0.7M by 2027 and +2.1M 2032-36, GLE up to 6M from 2030, Orano 7.4M 2032-39).

TENEX Supply Contract runs through 2028 (non-US use after the US ban), Orano Supply Agreement through 2030 with annual minimums; LEU RPO $0.7B to 2030; ~25% gross margin less selling costs, after tax.
Paid ~$116M ($95M cash + $21M stock); revenue undisclosed; haircut 14% for oil & gas cyclicality and an 'adjusted EPS' accretion claim.
FY2025 TS gross profit $6.0M; ~5x.

inputs_detail.input: Corporate cost not in plant margins
inputs_detail.derivation: Centrus SG&A $36.2M + equity comp $5.8M (FY2025), rising in 2026; Urenco-like margins already carry ~6% of revenue overhead, so the excess public-company/SBC cost is ~$20M pre-tax x 0.79.
Bear weighted up for execution history and the Western supply wave; within-scenario vol 0.30 (89% realised equity vol is mostly between-scenario).
